characterization_methods.key_findings: Sample annealed 5 min shows equiaxed and fully recrystallised grains; grain size 25.2 ± 5.0 µm (SEM, Table 2).
characterization_methods.purpose: determine ferrite grain size of the annealed Fe-6.8Al samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: X-Pert PRO diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation
characterization_methods.key_findings: Micro-strain 9.46 × 10^-4 for 750 °C, 5 min; dislocation density ~6 × 10^12 m^-2 (decreases from ~2×10^15 m^-2 for 98% CR upon annealing); crystallite size not reported for the 5 min condition.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanned 40°–120°, step size 0.03°; only the (110) XRD peak profile used
characterization_methods.purpose: determine dislocation density (Variance method of Wilson and Groma), crystallite size and lattice micro-strain
characterization_methods.technique: X-ray diffraction (XRD) line-profile analysis / variance method

characterization_methods.key_findings: Dark-field image shows very fine ordered phase (bright) associated with dark background; ordered phase size determined as 2.1 ± 0.2 nm; diffraction pattern (inset) shows strong matrix spots and weak superlattice spots confirming ordered phase.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: dark-field imaging from weak superlattice diffraction spots; [011] zone axis
characterization_methods.purpose: detect and measure distribution and size of the ordered phase in Fe-6.8Al
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (dark-field TEM) with selected-area diffraction

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source, transmission geometry
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-6.8Al spectrum deconvoluted into five components (B_hf = 32.68, 30.34, 27.69, 25.05, 23.26 T) with assignments; peak ~23 T interpreted as possible low-volume-fraction Fe3Al phase. NOTE: measured on powder samples annealed at 600 °C for 60 min.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; velocity calibrated with pure α-Fe foil; fitted by NORMOS program
characterization_methods.purpose: examine local atomic configurations / ordered phase (DO3, B2) formation in Fe-Al alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Weak nano-sized ordered phase peak between q = 0.3–3 nm^-1; Fe3Al ordered phase diameter increased from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm with increasing Al content (Fe-6.8Al between these values). NOTE: measured on powder samples annealed at 600 °C for 60 min.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm, q-range 0.0254–10 nm^-1, transmission geometry, 4–6 h measurement; local mono-disperse model fitting with Eq. (2)
characterization_methods.purpose: quantify size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered DO3 phase

analytical_models.model_note: Solid solution strengthening for Fe-6.8Al calculated as 95.6 MPa; increases from 67.8 to 127.2 MPa for 5 to 9 wt% Al.

analytical_models.equation_role: calculates lattice frictional stress for dislocation glide on slip plane (Eq. 10)
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. (10) gives lattice frictional stress at 0 K; a room-temperature value of 41 MPa (from Speich and Swann, 0.4 wt% C-steel) was used due to lack of Fe-Al data.

analytical_models.equation_role: calculates strengthening from ordered phase formation (Eq. 11)
analytical_models.model_note: Uses ordered phase size and volume fraction determined by TEM and SAXS.

analytical_models.equation_role: calculates grain size / grain boundary strengthening (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.model_note: kHP for 99.95% pure iron was used; grain size determined by SEM for the annealed samples.
Dislocation density from the variance method applied to the (110) XRD peak profile.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism modelling (decomposition of yield strength into five mechanisms: dislocations, grain size, ordered phase, solid solution, lattice frictional stress)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Summed model contributions compared with the measured tensile yield strength (700 MPa for 750 °C, 5 min) as shown in Fig. 9.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation–ordered phase interaction (antiphase boundary / super-partial dislocation shearing)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Strengthening from ordered phase formation is attributed to the difference in separation of partial dislocations in ordered vs disordered phase, creating an antiphase boundary bounded by leading (destroys order) and trailing (restores order) dislocations; this constrains dislocations to travel in pairs, restricting mobility and increasing flow stress.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Recrystallization completed upon annealing at 750 °C for 5 min; ordering (formation of nano-sized Fe3Al) occurs, with higher extent of ordering after longer annealing.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocations constrained to travel in pairs within the ordered phase (splitting into super-partial dislocations); high-angle grain boundaries arrest dislocation motion.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength and elongation (YS = 700 MPa, elongation = 20% rival those of dual-phase low-density steels)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Charges of interstitial free (IF) steel and pure aluminium melted in a vacuum arc furnace to prepare the low-density steel with 6.8 wt% Al; circular buttons (diameter 10 cm, height 5 cm) re-melted 7–8 times to remove segregation.

The Fe-6.8Al alloy was cold rolled to 98% reduction in thickness. Cold rolled sample shows heavily elongated + pancaked grains along RD with shear bands (~40° to RD); average deformed lamellae width 2.6 ± 1.2 µm.
Annealed at 750 °C for 5 min, producing equiaxed and fully recrystallised ferrite grains; recrystallization is already completed upon annealing for 5 min.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests in an Instron 5967 screw driven machine; three tensile tests conducted for each sample condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: sub-size tensile specimen, gauge length 6 mm and width 2 mm; gauge section machined parallel to rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: Rate of strain hardening vs true strain (Fig. 8b, red 5 min curve): steep initial spike followed by a small local maximum near true strain ~0.02 then monotonic decay; the 60 min curve lies above the 5 min curve at all strains.
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for the 5 min sample (red curve, Fig. 8a): yields near 700 MPa, plateaus to a broad maximum near 860–870 MPa between ~15 and 20% strain, then softens, terminating close to the 30% strain gridline.

phases_present.morphology: nano-sized ordered phase (bright particles in dark-field TEM, associated with dark background)

precipitates.distribution: very fine ordered phase (bright) dispersed in the Fe-Al matrix, seen associated with dark background in dark-field TEM; SAXS shows nano-sized ordered phase peak between q = 0.3–3 nm^-1

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed and fully recrystallised ferrite grains after 98% cold rolling + annealing at 750 °C for 5 min; single ferrite (BCC) phase stabilised by Al addition, containing a nano-sized Fe3Al ordered phase.

unmapped_findings: Yield ratio (YS/UTS) of the Fe-6.8Al sample annealed at 750 °C for 5 min = 0.85 (Table 4).

Strengthening contributions to the yield strength (Fig. 9) for 750 °C, 5 min (total YS = 700 MPa): grain boundary strengthening (dominant, up to ~500 MPa), followed by nearly equal contributions from dislocations (~650 MPa cumulative) and ordered Fe3Al phase; solid solution up to ~120 MPa; lattice frictional stress constant.
For the fully recrystallised 750 °C, 5 min sample the contributions order is: grain size strengthening (dominant), then nearly equal contributions from dislocations and ordered Fe3Al phase.
Dislocation density drops rapidly (about three orders of magnitude) from ~2.2 × 10^15 m^-2 (98% CR) to ~6 × 10^12 m^-2 (750 °C, 5 min) and ~1 × 10^12 m^-2 (60 min) upon annealing at 750 °C.

The Fe-6.8Al single ferrite phase was confirmed by XRD; Rietveld refinement (MAUD) was performed; the lattice micro-strain decreases sharply from 98% CR (1.46 × 10^-3) to 750 °C, 5 min (9.46 × 10^-4) and 750 °C, 60 min (1.46 × 10^-4) due to recrystallization.
Crystallite size (102.3 ± 9.8 nm) is reported only for the 98% CR condition (XRD); it is not reported for the 750 °C, 5 min condition (marked '-' in Table 3).
The ordered phase was characterized as nano-sized Fe3Al with DO3 structure; ordered phase sizes range between 2.5 and 3.75 nm (SAXS) and 2.1 ± 0.2 nm (TEM) increasing with Al content.
